Measurement-Oriented Microscopy Reconstruction
for Cross-Magnification Micro-Displacement Inspection

name: intro_body
text:
Optical inspection estimates motion from image features. A sharper reconstructed edge is useful when its measured position remains stable. Optical blur, pixel sampling and reconstruction-induced boundary shifts can all change the reported displacement, especially when an inspection workflow switches objectives.

MOSR combines U-Net context [1], calibrated optical guidance and anti-aliased processing [2] to address these effects. Bounded correction retains the original image grid and limits geometry changes while improving boundary visibility. One fixed set of learned weights serves both objectives.

At a common nominal step of 1 µm, this study compares Raw, fixed Wiener and MOSR at 20× and 50×. Each condition contributes 30 measured single steps. The central outcome is the variation of these steps, linking reconstruction quality directly to displacement measurement.

name: methods_body
text:
Data and reconstruction. Each objective contributes 30 adjacent-frame displacements at a 1 µm nominal step. MOSR uses fixed weights and native-grid outputs, with 25 measured PSF kernels at 20× and one calibrated kernel at 50×. Fixed Wiener uses a regularization value of 0.0565.

Boundary and center. A coarse active contour [3] initializes each pillar boundary. Intensity profiles normal to the contour use 0.1-pixel spacing. Quadratic refinement locates each gradient maximum between samples. Geometric least-squares circle fitting [4] uses 64 refined points at 20× and 96 at 50× to estimate the center.

Displacement and statistics. Nine pillar-center changes produce one step through their median along the acquisition motion direction. Object-space conversion uses the scale in Table I. Each condition yields one sample SD from its 30 steps. Raw, Wiener and MOSR share the same images, features and center-calculation settings.

name: conclusions_body
text:
MOSR reduces the SD of 30 measured single steps by 57.2% at 20× and 23.5% at 50×, at a common nominal step of 1 µm. Each result retains its own acquisition condition.

One reconstruction model supports both objectives with calibrated optical inputs. Clearer boundaries and lower step variation support cross-magnification optical inspection.

20x: September 3 thesis run 003412_XY_0, acquisition run 7, the first evaluation run after the existing first-six-RAW-scan direction calibration split. Use all 31 frames and all 30 adjacent steps. This presentation selection follows the user request after full 30-scan auditing and is not a preregistered original-study choice.
50x: July 2 original 1 micrometer cohort, all 30 original Raw-locked adjacent pairs, ordered by acquisition index. They are selected pairs rather than a new 31-frame scan.
Each headline is 100*(1-SD(MOSR)/SD(Raw)), using sample SD of exactly 30 image-measured steps in that condition. There is no pooled scan statistic and no cross-objective average on this poster.
Curve values are observed image-measured displacements minus nominal 1000 nm, with identical axes in both plots. No per-method recentering, detrending, scaling, clipping or outlier removal is applied.
The complete 30-scan 20x study and 0.5 micrometer 50x result remain in the supplementary records. The submitted two-page manuscript is unchanged.
Both methods use the same normal-gradient geometric LSC family with the same settings within each condition. The submitted manuscript supplies references [1]-[4].
